reviews.review: ok, so personally after completing the demo I wanted to run more and more of the game to see its depth and expansion it looked like it was building towards. it is a dungeon crawler with rouge lite mechanics, it has a lot of going in and leaving early so that the next dive gets both easier and faster for the following runs. Gameplay so far does feel stiff as the demo is the very beginning of the game rather than the later half of the game, it relies more on the player able to keep pace with the different mechanics that is thrown at you but if you do not have experience with this type of game it is a lot and they try to space out everything for you to chew through it. The design is one of my favorite parts with both writing and design going over the top for a really crazy story line so it never takes itself too seriously. Like other reviews for the demo flying enemies are a problem with no real air combos or options outside of certain forms, and no lock on can make the camera lose what is going on when there is a lot of enemies. The forms themselves open up different gameplays and can fall off when diving deeper meaning you would need to be on your toes when your favorite form is gone and something is better than nothing. The parry is also a risky move in that it takes some of your health in order to use it and it can be used to cancel any attack your doing but using it over and over can have consequences. Overall I think a solid game that feeds into its own cycle but not for everyone of course, I loved the demo and can not wait for the full release.

Did a few runs, unlocked quite a few things. not sure how many things left if any is there for me to unlock in this demo but i think i've seen enough to form an opinion.

- World building is amazing. 
i love the concept, the idea, story, even protagonist motivation. 
game does not take itself too seriously, it tries to go for that goofy approach but you can see that people put serious effort in it. it is all well thought out.

- characters are ironically full of life
each character has personality and they all have their own goals and interests leading to interesting clash of characters that liven up the story. reason i say the characters are ironically full of life is because we are talking about monsters and zombies :D. also were-chihuahua is just too perfect concept to be ignored :D

- game mechanics
well, its another roguelike hack and slash kinda game. i enjoyed hades and hades two and this feels like it fits right down that alley. go out kill enemies, fight bosses. unlock new stuff, get stronger, go again, take a step further, rinse and repeat... its grindy but its a demo so i am hoping full game will bring more worlds and more versatility to balance it out.

right now there is two worlds, or at least if there is third i did not get to it yet. bosses are interesting, boss fights are okay, i would not got as far as to say they are challenging but you can at least feel like you are fighting a boss.

my overall enjoyment is pretty high, i'd give it 8/10 so far. i am definitely looking forward to full game and i already prepurchased it. 
Biggest issue i had with in the demo is the aerial combat. harpies were real pain to deal with and full game will have to fix this in some way, i am guessing they will add lock in system so that dave faces the locked enemy regardless where he is. right now its too annoying.
other than that, i really have no complains. promising game with solid demo and very fun story concept.

I didn't realize that this was a roguelite, so I take part of the blame for my expectations being dashed. I'd be kinder towards this game if it was the linear sort of action title that the trailers make it out to be; as is, this is in competition with some truly stellar games while also being twice the price at minimum. 

Like many others say, this does feel like an older gen title, something that you'd see on the Xbox 360, and not entirely in a bad way. However, Stupid Never Dies can't pick a lane between yapping nonstop and being an okay beat 'em up. The writing and premise are by far the spots that shine brightest here, but when you're selling yourself on combat first and foremost, very, very lengthy yap sessions where people repeat themselves over and over grows long in the tooth, quickly.

If you're kinder towards experimentation, have plumbed out the genre, or simply have a bigger checkbook, then I'd say give it a go if you really feel like it. For myself, though, this is a buy only on sale.

Stupid Never Dies caught my attention from its first reveal trailer and I could not wait to get my hands on it, a few days ago they put out a demo and I fell in love with this game.

Stupid Never Dies is such a breath of fresh air for me, from the forward messy momentum of combat, the variety in combat Styles, and the absolute bombardment of personality in all of the little things makes this game a treat if you let them take you on the ride.

COMBAT - The combat in this game while simple on the surface, begs you to embrace the messy momentum and follow the rhythms that present themselves to you. The combat has so much weight to it that every hit feels so meaty and meaningful, my god kicking enemies into walls or off the map as Davy was deeply satisfying.

Everything in this game wants you to go forward, the teddy timer ever present on your screen during a run, the bite mechanic can be used to restore some health incentivizing you to rush down enemies even at low health, the “stupid parry” as they call it moves you forward, and there is no locking onto enemies which I think is maybe the biggest design choice that supports this forward momentum and I love it. Having a lock on would go against the overall gamefeel the game is presenting. Having no lock on frees you up to be loose, and when an enemy turns gold for a heavy attack you can more easily pursue that opportunity. Sure you can try to prioritize what enemies to kill like you might in other action games but I think that singular way of thinking isn’t what everything in this game is telling me to do, wailing on enemies indiscriminately, biting cores as they come, seizing opportunities to parry, and keeping an eye out for when to use your consumable abilities feels more in line with the mechanical themes of this game.

Kill fast, get hit, get health back from biting enemies and leveling up, and rip those abilities when they refresh. Learning my move set was such a joy, figuring out how to chain together moves, hit clusters of flying enemies, and swapping between Styles is a dance that I am so excited to learn more of in the full game. The body mods allow for flexible builds that help you dispose of enemies in a way that fits you, you can unlock multiple slots to have presets for your run, and switch out to other presets mid run at landing areas. Understanding my moves better led to me being able to chain together normal attacks and abilities to stay airborne longer to deal with Harpies, not being magnetized to enemies like you might find in other games made me consider the cost of my combos, abilities, and positioning in a fresh way.

I also really love the movement options each Style presents you with, being able to do some wall jumps with the Werewolf or fly with the Harpy to get extra goodies adds another layer of interactivity to the world that is much appreciated, especially considering I was already looking up and around all the time given my fascination with the warped and vertical environments.

AESTETHIC - I absolutely love this games art style, they struck a beautiful balance of soft colors but not incredibly muted, meaning that when the vibrant colors splash all over the screen they contrast and overlay quite nicely into a visual feast.

The mixed media elements go such a long way, photo scans of people, places, items, the scribbly drawings that pop up in flashbacks and when Davy goes berserk. Even the little touch of Davy moving at a lower framerate in this flashback.

I love shopping malls in games so the hub area being one made me really excited, each character having their own little area with their own music made zooming around on the little robot so much fun. Davy is super slow in the hub world which I thought the Doctor was gonna fix by giving us exoskeleton legs or something but no, he just tells us to sit on the roomba looking robot when we wanna go fast. Seeing Davy’s arms flail about is another great touch.

Each menu being given so much love in it’s presentation, adding a tactile distinction that helped me remember who I go to for what.

I love these characters, I know some people won’t care for them but I love them all, I didn’t skip any of the dialogue, I found myself continuously laughing over how silly the character interactions are. The goofy and unself serious writing paired with all of the voice actors absolutely nailing the delivery of these lines had me grinning the whole time I played, my face was hurting because I just couldn’t stop smiling. The sound board esc sounds popping up in conversation never got old.

The story itself so far is straight forward, but presented in a way that keeps me engaged. The story feels like eating sour candy, I’m familiar with the taste but in the moments of the flavor bursting through I always get lost in the joy of experience.

Anyways, I recommend this demo so hard.

The plot is interesting, but its only and biggest flaw is the inability to fix the attack direction. Currently, it's basically impossible to fight aerial units. Jumping to attack has a very low hit rate, and it's difficult to determine the attack location without facing the screen. Jumping and punching empty air will still result in getting hit. Even slight movement on the ground causes the attack to deviate drastically, especially when transformed into a birdman. Even if the enemy is clearly in front of you, dodging the attack will result in hitting nothing at all. A function should be added that allows the character to keep attacking while facing directly in front of the screen.

- Hello. I'm a zombie. I'm gonna save my (not) girlfriend. I need to defeat KOM.
- You will not defeat KOM. KOM is the strongest and you are a zombie, the weakest.
- You don't understand. I'm a zombie and I need to defeat KOM.

And it repeats these three bits of info ad infinitum.

[b]Pros[/b]
- Phenomenal art style, music, and general vibes.

- The story is quirky, cheeky, and  goofy; in a good way! 

- The systems all seem relatively deep and varied, hopefully that translates into a game with a long-tail in terms of gameplay.

- Overall, I think there's a ton of potential here and if the small number of pain points are ironed out it will be a great game.

[b]Cons[/b]
- The lack of any real targeting/lock-on system really hurts the combat, especially when dealing with harpies. The game needs something akin to Arkham Asylum, Dark Souls, or something in between to ensure combat doesn't feel frustrating for all the wrong reasons.

- The pacing of the introduction is really bad. The ratio of dialogue/menu popups to gameplay is mind-numbing, and I say that as someone who actually finds the dialogue largely amusing. Pulling the player out of their run prematurely so many times just to dump exposition and/or systems info at them feels very disruptive and unpleasant. 

- Unless the two points above get addressed, I personally don't see myself snagging this game anytime soon. Though, to be fair for the type of game it seems to be $50 is a steep ask, IMO. I'll keep tabs on it and see if they address these pain points that seem to show up a lot in the reviews I've read.

Serei simples e rápido falando sobre essa Demo, pois me vi surpreso, inicialmente o jogo me chamou atenção pela estética estilo Suda51, mas a gameplay me preocupava porém estou muito feliz que essa Demo sanou minhas dúvidas.

História: Pelo que foi mostrado na Demo a história desse jogo será interessante e divertida podendo ser até talvez comovente? Não sei ao certo, mas a Demo me deixou muito curioso para o jogo final.

Gameplay: A gameplay pelo que joguei esta incrível, divertida, frenética é bem intensa como eu gosto bastante.

Roguelike?: Bem esse jogo tem características semelhantes a um roguelike sim, porem diria que a maneira como organizam tudo faz as coisas serem bem mais interessantes, em especial as progressão acelerada que o jogo mostra como dinâmica base me fez realmente ficar bem positivo, pois pessoalmente roguelike não me agrada muito, mas nesse jogo não senti nenhum incômodo foi uma gameplay super divertida de ter.

Música: As musicas do jogo são muito boas, a música principal que toca no menu principal é muito boa e até gruda na cabeça e as músicas de batalhas e chefes também são muito boas.

Lobisomem: Sim aqui tem um jogo onde você pode pegar um poder de se transformar em lobisomem e lutar como um, uma coisa rara e que é muito divertido de fazer no jogo, muito obrigado por colocar essa transformação no jogo, agora finalmente vou ter um jogo que posso virar lobisomem e batalhar de forma épica, e nem preciso falar que quando o jogo sair vou fazer de tudo para transformar o lobisomem na transformação mais forte, pelo menos tenho certeza que vai se a que mais vou usar.

Por fim, não me estenderei muito aqui pois é só uma demo, uma das melhores demos que tem na steam, nela você pode ter certeza real se o jogo funciona ou não com você e isso é o tipo ideal de demonstração que deveriam ser feitas, tendo dito isso agora vou ficar olhando no relógio e contando os dias para o lançamento do jogo, antes já queria ele, agora pretendo comprar de imediato pois essa demo me deu a confiança de que o produto final terá qualidade, agora é esperar esses dias até o lançamento para saber como a história vai se desenrolar e para poder jogar como lobisomem novamente.

大枠としては、拠点に戻ってのプレイヤー強化を繰り返していくタイプのローグライト。
ストーリーはギャグ寄りに若干突き抜けているが体験版範囲では滑ってる感じはない。
戦闘面についてはゾンビと言う設定を活かしてダメージを気合で耐えては敵に噛み付いてリゲインしたり相手の能力を奪ったり、拠点の強化やダンジョン内の3択パッシブで特定の方向に寄せたビルドを作っていくことになるようなので期待できそう。

[hr][/hr][h3]恒久強化[/h3]
時間制限ありのダンジョンアタックを繰り返す過程でプレイヤーの装備（パッシブやらアクティブやらが付属）を集めたり、ダンジョン中に3択で取れるパッシブがアンロックされたり、レベルアップ速度（ダンジョンに潜る度レベル1から始まる）が上がったりしていく。

体験版範囲ではそこまでレア度の高い装備は取れていないが、いずれ拠点で設定した装備とダンジョン内のパッシブとで特定の方向に寄せたビルドを作っていくのだろう。
また、ダンジョン中でも定期的に挟まる休憩エリアではあらかじめ用意しておいた装備プリセットに変更できるので、ダンジョン内でのパッシブの引きに合わせて装備側のビルドを変えることもできるらしい。
そしてレベルアップ速度についてはステータス強化が早まるだけでなく、レベルアップ時に発生するかなり高ダメージの衝撃波の頻度も上がっていく。

これらの合わせ技によって、ダンジョンアタックを繰り返すにつれて制限時間の中でもどんどん早く深く潜れるようになっていくのだろう。
[hr][/hr][h3]戦闘[/h3]
特徴的なシステムとして「ステューピッドパリィ」と「バイト」というものがある。

前者は例のごとく相手の攻撃にタイミングを合わせて使う防御アクション（強力な反撃への派生可能）だが、このアクションはダメージを完全に無効化するわけではなくあくまで軽減するだけになっている。（HPが0にならないのでゲームが進むと軽減しても即死、なんてことにはならない）
そしてこのゲームには回避やカット率100%のガードはないので、立ち位置で回避できない攻撃はこれで受けることになる。

しかしバイトで相手に噛み付くことで自分が受けたばかりのダメージ（のうち一定割合？）を一気に回復できるようになっている。
そのため防御面についてはある程度は立ち位置で回避しつつも避けられない攻撃（もしくは反撃狙い）はパリィで受けつつ、返しのバイトで一気に体力を回復するという流れになるのだろう。

じゃあ戦闘がスローペースかと言われるとボスについてはそうなのだが、道中の雑魚戦については割とファストペースが求められる。
というのも敵1人1人に向き合うには敵の数が割と多い。ゲームシステムとしてロックオンがないが、このシステムでロックオン用意してもな…と思えるぐらい。
なのでこちらはスタイルごとのアクティブスキルや持ち込みのアクティブスキル、さらには雑魚にバイトを当てて得られる使い切りスキルなどで雑に敵を吹き飛ばしていくことが求められているのだと思う。

一方でボスについては真っ当に敵の攻撃を立ち位置で避けたりパリィしたり、予兆付きの攻撃をパリィしてダウンっぽい感じにして反撃したりと硬派寄り。ご丁寧に雑魚も召喚してくれるので使い切りスキルも補充できる。
とはいっても体験版範囲だとスキル乱打で雑に殺せるし元々そういう想定かもしれない。

[hr][/hr][h3]ストーリー[/h3]
そもそもの導入が「見ず知らずの凍死体に一目惚れしたゾンビが、なんやかんやでその凍死体を蘇生するためにダンジョンアタックを繰り返す」という話なので大分ギャグに寄っている。
ゲームシステム的にも、ダンジョンパワーで強化されるダンジョン以外ではのろまなのでロボット掃除機に乗って移動したり、ダンジョンに潜る入口がトイレだったりとそういうノリ。
とはいっても体験版範囲だと「過度なギャグや下品なギャグで滑ってる」という感じもなく、ちゃんと好感を持てるぐらいのギャグ配分。

また、真面目なお話的にも「かつて人間vsモンスターの戦争から逃げてクソビビりと馬鹿にされてきたゾンビが、見ず知らずの女性のために一念発起して女性を蘇らせる（ついでに世界も救う）」という話なので、そっち方面でもちゃんと頑張ってくれそうな気配を感じる。
